newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: TRAWLER IN DANGER OF BREAKING UP AFTER RUNNING-AGROUND
A cray boat, which had three fishermen onboard, is still being battered by strong winds on rocks near Apollo Bay, in south-western Victoria.
The 20-metre trawler became stranded at low tide, about 100 metres off-shore at Cape Patton early this morning.
Two men have made it to shore, but the skipper is staying on-board.
There are fears the vessel could break up in the windy conditions, but a tow boat is expected to arrive shortly.
Brian Brady, who is involved in the salvage operation, says the alarm was raised just after five o'clock.
COMPANY PARTLY CONTROLLED BY HAWKE MAKES BIG PROPERTY SALE
A property, partly owned by former Prime Minister, Bob Hawke, has sold in Melbourne for more than $15.5 million.
The 10-storey "Hothlyn House" in Collins Street was sold to an undisclosed consortium.
Bundeway, a company controlled by investor Peter Bartholoemew and Mr Hawke, bought the property in 1993 for $7.2 million.
Real Estate agents say the sale reflects the bouyancy of the Australian property market.
The Collins Street building is occupied by Telstra, Qantas, American Express and Wilson Parking.
NLC: NT LAND RIGHTS PAY-OFF A DUD FOR ABORIGINES
The Northern Land Council says one of the trade-offs for the sunset clause in the Northern Territory Land Rights Act has not delivered much for Aboriginal people.
The clause, inserted after a review of the act, effectively closed off the lodgement of new land claims, by denying them a hearing by the Aboriginal Land Commissioner.
The land council's Norman Fry says the trade-off involved the Community Living Areas Act which was supposed to give traditional owners living areas excised from pastoral leases.
But he says it has never been allowed to work properly, because of Ministerial interventions.
BASKETBALL: MEN AND WOMEN QUALIFY FOR WORLD CHAMPS
The Australian men's and women's basketball teams have qualified for next year's World Championships.
At the Oceania qualifying tournament in New Zealand, both teams had wins over the host nation - the men winning 85-67 and the women 99 to 61.
Shane Heal top-scored for the Boomers with 20 points and Andrew Gaze got 19.
For the Opals, Rachel Sporn and Allison Cook both scored 22 points.
VIC TO PUSH FOR DROPPING OF FRUIT BANS
Victoria will be pushing for the dropping of restrictions on its apples and pears at a meeting of Agriculture Ministers in Canberra today.
Victorian Minister, Pat McNamara, has been lobbying interstate agriculture and quarantine specialists to re-open interstate borders.
The latest tests in Germany are yet to find proof the destructive fire blight disease actually exists in Victoria.
Mr McNamara says Victorian producers have been disadvantaged for long enough, and is pushing for states which did introduced bans to lift them by Friday.
TAX INCREASES IN NSW UNDER FIRE
The New South Wales Government is coming under pressure from a range of business groups as the July first implementation date for many of its tax increases draws nearer.
Parking station operators have joined the tourism and hotel lobby as well as the club movement in harshly criticisin the state budget.
Parking station operators have written to their clients advising that rates for permanent parking spots will rise by $17 a month because of the doubling of the parking space levy in Sydney.
People who park in the city on a casual basis will pay about an extra dollar a day.
